name: Google Coral Edge TPU
memory_type: On-chip SRAM (8 MB); no external DRAM on the ASIC
memory_bandwidth_basis: Edge TPU is an INT8 vision accelerator with no LLM-relevant memory-bandwidth figure published in a form comparable to GPU VRAM bandwidth; it runs LiteRT/EdgeTPU-compiled CNNs, not transformer decode.

flops.basis_detail: Google Coral Edge TPU: 4 TOPS INT8, vendor-published. This is a vision/camera inference figure, not an LLM path.

notes: PAPERWEIGHT for LLM. Coral is an INT8-only VISION accelerator (~4 TOPS). The whole stack is LiteRT/EdgeTPU-compiled CNNs - classification, detection, pose, segmentation. There is NO LLM serving path, no transformer-decode support, no int4/GGUF story; 4 TOPS INT8 cannot hold a 7B weight set let alone stream one. Used units trade at $50-130 and are often bundled cheap with other gear. Fine for a camera/detection project; do not buy it expecting language models. || Filled 2026-10-19: Google documents an 8 MB on-chip SRAM scratchpad and no external memory interface, so 0.008 GB is the entire memory system. Google publishes no bandwidth figure for the SRAM, so bandwidth is null rather than derived.
